story: Kodiak's isolated island microgrid faces a Navy building the service says is not a data center, and the utility's 2 MW number is its own estimate because the Navy gave it none

claims.claim: The U.S. Navy is building what it calls a multi-mission support building at its Special Warfare Center Detachment on Spruce Cape in Kodiak.
claims.verbatim: the U.S. Navy is constructing what it calls a, "multi-mission support building" at its Special Warfare Center Detachment on Spruce Cape in Kodiak
claims.notes: SINGLE OUTLET. DVIDS, HigherGov, sullivan.senate.gov, Alaska Public Media and Alaska Beacon carry nothing on this facility. Kodiak Daily Mirror returned HTTP 429 on four attempts.

claims.claim: Navy spokesperson Lt. Samuel Hardgrove told KMXT by email on August 14th that the operational facility is not a data center.
claims.verbatim: But Hardgrove told KMXT via email on Aug.14 that the operational facility is, "not a data center."
claims.notes: The verified fact is that the Navy SAID this, never that it is true or false. Always an attributed denial.

claims.claim: Hardgrove said the new facility will be powered from the existing power grid and will have back-up generators.
claims.verbatim: He also said that the new facility will be powered from the existing power grid, although it will have back-up generators.
claims.notes: The load-bearing detail. The Navy itself says the building draws on the cooperative's grid, which is what makes the utility's estimate matter.

claims.claim: Kodiak Electric Association CEO Dan Menth said the Navy has not told the utility specifically how much power the new facility will use.
claims.verbatim: Menth said the Navy has not told the local utility specifically how much power the new facility will use.
claims.notes: THE SPINE. Pair with C05 always.

claims.claim: Kodiak Electric Association expects the Navy's future energy demand could be up to an additional two megawatts at its Kodiak detachment, according to a utility planning document.
claims.value: up to an additional two megawatts
claims.verbatim: But KEA expects the Navy's future energy demand could be up to an additional two megawatts at its Kodiak detachment, according to a utility planning document.
claims.notes: ESTIMATE, NOT MEASUREMENT, and not a Navy figure. Write "as much as 2 MW", never a flat 2 MW. The planning document is not named, dated or linked and the studio has not read it.

claims.claim: Kodiak Electric Association almost had to start diesel generators in March when the peak load hit just over 31 MW.
claims.verbatim: which the cooperative almost had to do in March when the peak load hit just over 31 MW
claims.notes: NO YEAR IS STATED ON THE PAGE. Write "in March" and stop. A year is an inference and the fact-checker killed it.

claims.claim: Kodiak's micro-grid generates nearly 100 percent of its power from renewable energy sources.
claims.verbatim: Kodiak's limited micro-grid, which generates nearly 100% of its power from renewable energy sources
claims.notes: Corroborated in magnitude by the cooperative's own 98 percent goal at C22.

claims.claim: Kodiak Electric Association owns, operates and maintains an isolated grid.
claims.verbatim: KEA owns, operates, and maintains an isolated grid.
claims.notes: PRIMARY, the utility's own words. Say isolated. Do NOT write that the grid can't import power, because no source uses that construction.

claims.claim: Terror Lake Hydroelectric plant provides approximately 85 percent of Kodiak Electric Association's generation.
claims.verbatim: the primary being Terror Lake Hydroelectric plant providing approximately 85% of our generation
claims.notes: PRIMARY. Undated evergreen page, so the share is current but unstamped.

claims.claim: The rest of Kodiak Electric Association's generation comes from six wind turbines, two flywheels and a battery energy storage system, with diesel generation kept as back up.
claims.verbatim: The remaining generation is provided by a combination of six wind turbines, two flywheels and a battery energy storage system. KEA also maintains diesel generation facilities as back up.
claims.notes: PRIMARY, and it independently corroborates the turbine count.

claims.claim: Pillar Mountain has six wind turbines each generating 1.5 MW.
claims.verbatim: wind turbines on Pillar Mountain, which features six turbines total, each generating 1.5 MW
claims.notes: Turbine count corroborated by the cooperative at C10. The 1.5 MW rating is KMXT only. Nameplate is 9 MW.

claims.claim: One of the six Pillar Mountain turbines has been offline since March of 2025.
claims.verbatim: but one of those has been offline since March of 2025
claims.notes: The cooperative's own site says six turbines and does not report an outage, so the utility does not corroborate this.

claims.claim: Kodiak Electric Association CEO Dan Menth said the cooperative didn't have to turn diesels on but that growing load could make it a potential.
claims.value: didn't have to turn diesels on
claims.verbatim: We didn't have to turn diesels on, but as the load continues to grow, that could certainly become a potential,
claims.notes: Quote ends on a comma before the attribution, reproduced exactly.

claims.claim: Sen. Dan Sullivan said he had never heard of it, that he thinks it is a rumor, and that if true it is a bad idea he would work to stop.
claims.verbatim: I've never heard of this. I think it's a rumor, but if it's true, I think it's a bad idea, and I will work to stop it,
claims.notes: SECOND HAND. Said to the Kodiak Daily Mirror on August 11th during a Kodiak visit, reported by KMXT. The originating outlet returned HTTP 429 on every attempt. The quoted string ends on a COMMA, not a period.

claims.claim: Sen. Sullivan's communications director Amanda Coyne said by email that the Navy has explicitly confirmed to Sullivan's office that the project is not a data center.
claims.verbatim: the Navy has explicitly confirmed to Sen. Sullivan's office that this project is not a data center.
claims.notes: A second channel for the same denial, still the Navy denying it. Murkowski's office told KMXT it had been told something similar with no further details.

claims.claim: A utility planning document cited by KMXT states that the new facility plus power needs from the expanding Coast Guard base and other island projects will exceed what Kodiak Electric Association can generate from its current renewable sources.
claims.verbatim: The document states that the new facility plus power needs from the expanding Coast Guard base and other projects on the island will exceed what KEA can generate through its current renewable energy sources.
claims.notes: SOFTEST CLAIM IN THE PACKAGE. A projection, inside a paraphrase of an unobtainable document. Always attributed, never standalone. It is the only support for the Coast Guard expansion.

claims.claim: Hardgrove said work at Spruce Cape will include site preparation, paving and site improvements, and construction of the building including electrical and mechanical subsystems.
claims.value: site preparation, paving and site improvements
claims.verbatim: site preparation, paving and site improvements, and construction of the building which include electrical and mechanical subsystems.
claims.notes: The only scope description the Navy gave. Nothing in it identifies compute, cooling or server capacity either way.

claims.claim: It is unclear when work on the new Spruce Cape facility will begin.
claims.verbatim: As of now, it's unclear when that work will begin.
claims.notes: The deck must NOT assert an imminent start. The scouts said about to begin and that is wrong.

claims.claim: The Naval Special Warfare Center on Spruce Cape has been in operation since 1987 according to state documents.
claims.verbatim: According to state documents, the Naval Special Warfare Center on Spruce Cape has been in operation since 1987.
claims.notes: BACKGROUND, outside the window. Label as background if used.

claims.claim: Roughly ten years ago the Naval Special Warfare Center Detachment Kodiak completed a 25,000 square foot expansion for SEAL qualification training.
claims.verbatim: Roughly 10 years ago, the Naval Special Warfare Center Detachment Kodiak completed a 25,000 square-foot expansion to accommodate growing participation in SEAL qualification training classes.
claims.notes: BACKGROUND, outside the window. Useful only as scale for what an expansion here has historically meant.

claims.claim: Sen. Lisa Murkowski requested $10,000 from a Senate subcommittee on June 4th for planning and design of a Navy operations facility inside Coast Guard Air Station Kodiak.
claims.verbatim: Senator Lisa Murkowski requested $10,000 for the planning and design of this Navy facility from a Senate subcommittee on June 4.
claims.notes: BACKGROUND. A DIFFERENT facility, sited inside Coast Guard Air Station Kodiak, not the Spruce Cape building. Do not conflate. The page states June 4 with no year. A planning and design line, never the project's price.

claims.claim: Kodiak Electric Association states its aim is to maintain 98 percent of energy sales with cost effective renewable power solutions.
claims.verbatim: Endeavor to maintain 98% of energy sales with cost effective renewable power solutions for the future of our members and the community.
claims.notes: PRIMARY. A stated GOAL, not a measurement. The same page gives over 95 percent by 2013 and 98 percent maintained by 2017, which are historical.

claims.claim: In March 2025 two of the six Pillar Mountain turbines were not functioning properly, the northernmost with a bad blade bearing and turbine number 1 with a bad pitch drive.
claims.verbatim: Two are not functioning properly
claims.notes: Showrunner verified after the fact-check, by direct fetch. Supporting verbatim for the faults, "The northernmost turbine has a bad blade bearing" and "turbine number 1, that has a bad pitch drive." This is the ORIGIN of C12's outage and it is the same month. It does NOT establish which one is still down today, so do not name the turbine still offline.

claims.claim: Each Pillar Mountain turbine generates up to 1.5 megawatts, and when all six are going that is enough to power roughly 450 Kodiak homes.
claims.verbatim: Each turbine on Pillar generates up to 1.5 megawatts of electricity. When all six are going, that's enough to power roughly 450 Kodiak homes
claims.notes: READ THIS CAREFULLY. The 450 homes is ALL SIX TURBINES TOGETHER, not one turbine. A first reading of the page had it as per turbine and that was wrong. Any per-turbine or per-megawatt figure derived from this is an AGGREGATE and must be declared in aggregates.json before it can be printed.

claims.claim: Kodiak Electric Association CEO Dan Menth said the Terror Lake hydroelectric turbines typically generate roughly 85 percent of Kodiak's energy and the Pillar Mountain wind turbines usually supply the rest.
claims.verbatim: Typically the hydroelectric turbines at Terror Lake generate roughly 85% of Kodiak's energy. Wind turbines on Pillar usually supply the rest.
claims.notes: Showrunner verified by direct fetch. This INDEPENDENTLY corroborates C09, the cooperative's own approximately 85 percent, from a different year and a different document, in the CEO's own voice.

claims.claim: Kodiak Electric Association's Terror Lake hydroelectric project began commercial operation in 1985.
claims.verbatim: began commercial operation in 1985
claims.notes: PRIMARY, the cooperative's own About Us page. Showrunner verified by direct fetch after the fact-check.

claims.claim: Kodiak Electric Association's Pillar Mountain wind project was initiated in 2009.
claims.verbatim: initiated in 2009
claims.notes: PRIMARY. Showrunner verified by direct fetch.

claims.claim: Kodiak Electric Association completed the Upper Hidden Basin Diversion Project in 2019.
claims.verbatim: completed in 2019
claims.notes: PRIMARY. Showrunner verified by direct fetch. A third renewable addition, useful for the build sequence.

claims.claim: Kodiak Electric Association achieved over 95 percent of its power generation from renewable sources by 2013 and maintained 98 percent by 2017.
claims.verbatim: over 95 percent of its power generation from renewable sources by 2013
claims.notes: PRIMARY. HISTORICAL figures, not current ones. The page pairs them with the 98 percent aim at C22. Do not present either as today's number.

killed.claim: Kodiak's March 2026 peak load was just over 31 MW
killed.why: The page says in March and never states a year. Survives as C06 without a year.

killed.claim: The Navy is about to begin construction at Spruce Cape
killed.why: The article says it is unclear when that work will begin. Imminence is unsupported.

killed.claim: Sen. Dan Sullivan told KMXT on September 3rd that he had never heard of it
killed.why: Wrong outlet and wrong date. The quote came from a Kodiak Daily Mirror interview on August 11th. The originating outlet returned HTTP 429 on four attempts.

killed.claim: The Sullivan quote ends with a period
killed.why: The page ends the quoted string on a comma before the attribution, and this quote will be set as display type.

killed.claim: The Navy facility will add 2 MW to Kodiak's grid
killed.why: Unit and certainty error. The utility expects demand could be up to an additional two megawatts, a ceiling estimate, and the Navy supplied no number at all. Asserting a flat 2 MW inverts the point of the story.

killed.claim: The Coast Guard base in Kodiak is expanding
killed.why: Stated only inside a paraphrase of an unobtainable utility planning document. Survives only inside C16.

killed.claim: Kodiak's grid cannot import power from anywhere
killed.why: No source says it. Use the word isolated, in the utility's own voice.

killed.claim: An independent second outlet confirms the Navy project
killed.why: It does not exist as far as could be reached. DVIDS, HigherGov, sullivan.senate.gov, Alaska Public Media all carry nothing; Alaska Beacon 403 and Kodiak Daily Mirror 429.

killed.claim: The utility planning document is a public document
killed.why: Not named, dated or linked, and the cooperative's site has no planning or board minutes route. The deck may say KMXT cites one and must not imply the studio read it.

killed.claim: The Navy facility is not a data center
killed.why: This is the Navy's assertion, not a verified fact. A denial is not evidence of absence, and the island rumor is not evidence of presence. Neither side is established.

sourcing_assessment: Publishable with one disclosure on the deck's face. The news spine is SINGLE OUTLET. Every event, quote and megawatt figure outside the utility's own site comes from KMXT, and no second outlet or primary document could be found despite trying DVIDS, HigherGov, sullivan.senate.gov, Alaska Public Media, Alaska Beacon, the Kodiak Daily Mirror and four search engines. What saves the package is that the argument does not rest on the news. It rests on the shape of the grid, and that part is PRIMARY in the utility's own words at C08, C09, C10 and C22. Three things a reader must be told. The 2 MW is the utility's own ceiling estimate from a document nobody outside the cooperative has read, and the Navy gave the utility no number, which is the story rather than a footnote. The Navy's denial is a denial and not a finding, and the rumor is a rumor and not a finding. The peak load month carries no year, so write in March and stop. Build no slide on the Coast Guard expansion or on any start date.
showrunner_additions: C23, C24 and C25 were fetched and verified by the showrunner after the fact-checker returned, from a March 14th, 2025 KMXT report the sweep had not surfaced. They are background rather than in-window, and C25 is the only claim in the package that corroborates the 85 percent share from a second document. C26 to C29 were fetched and verified by the showrunner from the cooperative's own About Us page. They give the deck a dated build sequence, 1985, 2009, 2019, entirely from a PRIMARY source. SEPARATELY AND DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED, a widely repeated detail that Terror Lake sits about 25 miles from the city of Kodiak and is reachable only by air or boat. It appeared in a search summary of a secondary encyclopaedia, it is NOT on the cooperative's own site, and no page carrying it was fetched. It is a good detail and it is not verified, so no slide may use it.
